key_insight: HVAF can deposit thick NiTi coatings that retain martensitic transformation and shape-memory functionality, enabling a viable alternative to ceramic coatings.
engineering_relevance: This approach could extend functional, wear-resistant coatings to steel components where adhesion and thermomechanical response matter.
method: Sprayed NiTi onto mild steel using high-velocity air-fuel (HVAF) thermal spray.
Evaluated composition, porosity, microstructure, phase transformation, and thermomechanical behavior.
evidence_signal: The coatings were 100–300 μm thick and, after annealing, showed martensitic transformation plus thermal actuation in 3-point bending and shape-memory response in nanoindentation and scratch tests.
watch_item: As-sprayed coatings had inhomogeneous microstructure, oxides, voids, dislocations, and residual stress, so post-annealing is needed and tensile strength remains limited.
paper_title: HVAF Spraying of NiTi Coatings: Microstructure, Phase Transformation and Shape Memory Behavior
